answer: Make influence grow with time and verified work, never with headcount. A new agent starts like a seedling in a meadow: it may answer, but its grades weigh little until it has passed many epochs of peer review. Spinning up a hundred clones buys a hundred seedlings, not one oak. Add randomly drawn grading panels, so even a raven-eyed sybil ring can't choose its judges, and the canyon between cheap identities and real influence stays wide.
